stylingSystem.honestAbsenceTreatment: NEVER a blank. Three layered mechanisms, all already factored out: (1) CHIPS - CHIP_UNAVAILABLE='UNAVAILABLE', CHIP_FIXTURE_LABEL, CHIP_NO_ADDRESS (format.ts:72-74), drawn by drawChipOnLineBox() (render.ts:451, exported). (2) FIXED REASON SENTENCES - the REASON map (format.ts:105-117) holds one plain sentence per context, e.g. noZoning='No zoning record on file for this parcel.', noSetbackRule='No setback rule on file; setbacks not specified or verified.', noStreet='No road node attaches to this parcel.', floodNotQueried='Flood data was not queried on this run.', setbacksConsumeLot, frontEdgeUnresolved, noAddress, noCountyName, noCaptureDate, imageryFetchFailed, registrationNotComputable. (3) A PROSE-HYGIENE GATE - sheetReason() (format.ts:142) accepts an upstream reason ONLY if isCleanReasonSentence() (format.ts:123) passes: must end in a period, <=12 words, NO colon anywhere, no machine-code pattern (MACHINE_CODE_RE format.ts:119), no nested parens. Otherwise the fixed fallback is substituted. A live sheet leaked a colon-delimited machine string on 2026-07-28 and the colon rule was added as a result (format.ts:129-132). SECTION 5: 'empty layers must look intentional' - swatch + sentence-case label + reason inline on the legend row, never a suppressed layer. Provenance rows for absent layers read source='unavailable', confidence='honest absence' (provenance.ts:73-77, :86-90).

reportRunPersistence.criticalCaveat: THE TABLE IS REAL BUT IT IS NOT THE PARCEL-EXPORT REPORT LEDGER. Primary key is (engagement_id, report_type) - reportRun.ts pk: primaryKey({ columns: [t.engagementId, t.reportType] }). It is keyed by ENGAGEMENT (the AEC-cortex plan-review path), not by parcelNodeId. Its report_type vocabulary is the plan-review set only: compliance, topography, drainage, hydrology, hazard, encumbrances, brief, subsurface, avm (planReviewBff.ts:129-139). NONE of the PE download-menu artifacts (site-plan, flood-drainage, dossier, terrain) appear in it.
reportRunPersistence.secondCaveat: It is explicitly declared run STATE, NOT a result store: reportRun.ts:35-39 'This table is run STATE, not a result store. The materialized report results still live where they already lived ... Large payloads are never duplicated here.' It exists to fix a multi-instance Cloud Run bug where a status GET landing on a different instance saw 'not-run'. It is not a report ledger and does not persist a report run for audit.
reportRunPersistence.mcpFinding: `git grep -rn -iE 'report_run|reportRun|report-run' origin/main -- src` in P:/hauska-mcp-server returns ZERO hits. The MCP reporting gate has no report-run persistence at all.
reportRunPersistence.whatActuallyPersistsForPE: The parcel-terrain-model ATOM carries an artifacts map (author.ts:606 dxf-site-plan, :617 ifc-site-plan, :630 pdf-site-plan; flood-drainage-author.ts:143 pdf-flood-drainage, :154 json-flood-drainage-study). Client-side, the PE dossier stores an exports[] entry per (kind, format) with a re-download path and savedAt (P:/hauska-map/apps/property-explorer/src/workbench/tools/reports-dossier.ts:26 exportEntryFromResult) - and it explicitly stores NO bytes. And the Reports dock persists the last terminal export snapshot per property via useDockToolState (ReportsTool.tsx:57-61). So there IS artifact persistence, but there is NO run-level ledger for the parcel report surface.
reportRunPersistence.verdict: The Cortex charter sentence 'persists report runs' is TRUE for the plan-review/engagement surface in legacy-design-tools and FALSE for the parcel/PE report surface a feasibility study would live on. A feasibility-study spec must not assume it inherits report-run persistence.

Drawing a stroke at or above the property line's 1.6pt. SHEET STANDARD section 3 makes the property line the heaviest mark on any sheet.

Rendering an unavailable field as a blank, a dash, or 'N/A'. Section 5/6 require a chip plus a reason sentence from the REASON map, and isCleanReasonSentence() will reject any machine-shaped string (no colons, <=12 words, ends in a period).
Letting a machine identifier onto the sheet outside the provenance SOURCE column (section 11). sheetSafeStreetSource() exists solely because road-node ids leaked once.

Emitting a standalone page number stamp. Page numbering is a sentence in the fine-print run (buildFinePrint) and, in composed documents, flows through the SheetNumbering seam so appended site-plan sheets renumber correctly. A separate stamp would double-number the composed document.

Bypassing MarkRegistry when drawing repeated marks. Section 14 draw-once is enforced by keyed registration; a duplicate (page, kind, key) is silently dropped by design and re-implementing drawing without it reintroduces the double-bearing-tag bug.

Adding a NEW colour or type token to template-tokens.ts to serve the feasibility study specifically. That mutates the shared template and would propagate into the site plan and flood study - the literal thing the operator said not to touch.
realBlockersForFeasibilityStudy: ATOM REACH (severity: high). The MCP property-atom-chain exposes 3 slots of 16 registered types. Every atom family the statewide program has been building - flood-hazard-fact, special-district-fact, rail-corridor-fact, well-fact, rrc-pipeline-fact, utility-easement, owner-fact, land-use-fact, cad-parcel-roll - is unreachable to a report composer through that seam. A feasibility study is precisely a document that wants those. This must be widened before the study can be more than a restyled site plan.

NO FOOTPRINT (severity: medium-high for an architect/engineer audience). SitePlanModel has no footprint slot (zero grep hits in the whole site-plan directory), so no existing-structure layer can be drawn on PDF, DXF or IFC. building-footprint is a registered atom type with no path to the drawing.

VERCEL FUNCTION CAP (severity: medium). pe-site-plan-export.ts:17-19 records that dossier was folded in as a query param specifically to avoid a new serverless function against the 11/12 cap. The feasibility study must fold in the same way (a third query-param leg), not claim a route.

NO REPORT-RUN LEDGER ON THIS SURFACE (severity: medium). report_run is engagement-keyed plan-review run STATE in legacy-design-tools, not a parcel report ledger, and is explicitly not a result store. If the feasibility study needs an audit trail, it is new work.

TERRAIN IS PRO-ONLY (severity: low, but a pricing decision). Site-plan and flood sit in the $15 property unlock; terrain does not. Where a feasibility study lands is an unmade pricing call, and the gate is enforced server-side in two places (pe-site-plan-export.ts and pe-flood-drainage-core.ts) plus client-side in ReportsTool.tsx.

comparisonReportGroundwork.exists: PARTIALLY. P:/hauska-map/apps/property-explorer/src/workbench/tools/CompareTool.tsx + compare-facts.ts already implement a TWO-SLOT (a/b) comparison with 7 rows (COMPARE_ROWS, compare-facts.ts:118): zoning district, setbacks F/S/R, buildable, flood, land use, acreage, snapshot. Cells carry state present|absent|pending plus a per-fact source caption, and absent cells render the honest NOT_VERIFIED_HERE copy rather than a blank (compare-facts.ts:128-145).
comparisonReportGroundwork.gap: It is UI-ONLY. Grep for pdf/export/download in CompareTool.tsx returns no emitter. There is no comparison PDF, no engine-side comparison assembler, and the model is capped at two slots. A comparison REPORT would reuse COMPARE_ROWS and deriveCompareColumn as its data model and the provenance-table styling as its visual language, but the emitter is entirely new work.

adversarialFindings: STALENESS: 3 of 4 checkouts were NOT on main. hauska-map was on fix/console-derive-rail-list (31b4534) vs origin/main 848b6e2; legacy-design-tools on feat/s1-instrument-hardening (10069854) vs 48c4eb89; hauska-engine on a DETACHED HEAD at 89d4c08 vs 8d8e880 - i.e. the engine working tree does not even contain PR #315/#316/#317. Only hauska-mcp-server was clean on main. Every finding here was read via git show origin/main:<path>.

REPORT-RUN PERSISTENCE IS A CHARTER CLAIM THAT DOES NOT HOLD FOR THIS SURFACE. The Cortex definition says it 'persists report runs.' A report_run table genuinely exists (lib/db/src/schema/reportRun.ts, migration 0054) - but it is keyed (engagement_id, report_type) over the plan-review vocabulary only, its own doc comment says 'This table is run STATE, not a result store', and the MCP server has ZERO occurrences of report_run/reportRun anywhere in src. Nothing on the PE parcel export path writes a report run. Reporting the charter sentence as a live capability for the parcel surface would be exactly the instrument-not-data defect pattern.

ATOM-CHAIN SLOT LIST IS A HAND-MAINTAINED LITERAL WITH NO CROSS-REPO GUARD. PROPERTY_CHAIN_ENTITY_TYPES (hauska-mcp-server/src/property-atom-chain.ts:23) is declared independently of the engine's PROPERTY_ENTITY_TYPES (hauska-engine/packages/atoms/src/property-instances.ts:188). The engine list grew to 16 with a test asserting the count (parcel-node-registration.test.ts:64); the MCP list stayed at 4 and nothing detects the drift. Worse, the drift is DOUBLE-ENCODED: parcelNodeIdFromAtomDid() at property-atom-chain.ts:98 repeats the same four type names inside a regex, so widening the slot list alone would not widen DID resolution. Same failure shape as the has_writer hand-declaration finding.

THE 'DOWNLOAD MENU' IS NOT ONE MENU. The operator's mental model ('our list of download options') is three independently-gated sections in one dock bubble with two different format pickers, one fixed-format button, and a NINTH artifact (the dossier PDF) on a completely different surface (PropertyDossierDetail, not ReportsTool). Any spec that says 'add it to the download list' must name WHICH section, because the entitlement tier differs per section: site-plan and flood are in the $15 property unlock, terrain is Pro-only (ReportsTool.tsx:47,133).

THREE REPORTS SHARE ONE SERVERLESS FUNCTION BECAUSE OF A PLATFORM CAP, NOT BY DESIGN. pe-site-plan-export.ts:17-19 states the dossier was folded in via ?kind=dossier to avoid a new function against the Vercel 11/12 cap. vercel.json confirms only pe-site-plan-export and pe-terrain-export have rewrites. This is a real constraint on the new report and a fragility: one function now carries site-plan, flood-drainage and dossier, so a regression in its dispatch takes out all three.

SITE PLAN IS NOT RELIABLY 3 PAGES. TOTAL_SHEETS=3 is a floor; render.ts:193-194 explicitly warns 'Use countSitePlanSheets for the model-specific count; never assume 3' because overflow pagination inserts summary continuation sheets. A feasibility-study spec that appends the site-plan set and hard-codes 3 will mis-number every subsequent page. dossier.ts already handles this correctly via the SheetNumbering seam - copy that, do not re-derive it.

NO BUILDING FOOTPRINT ANYWHERE IN THE SITE-PLAN SURFACE. git grep -n -iE 'footprint' origin/main -- packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/ returns ZERO hits - not in site-model.ts, layout.ts, emitters.ts, render.ts, the tests, the fixtures, or SHEET_STANDARD_v1.html. building-footprint is registered as a property atom type but has no consumer in any deliverable. For a report aimed at architects and engineers this is the most consequential absence, and it is invisible from the docs.

THE STYLING SYSTEM IS THE STRONGEST ASSET AND IT IS PROPERLY DEFENDED. Unusually for this program, the claim checks out at the code level: a written 21-section standard (SHEET_STANDARD_v1.html), a single token module ported verbatim from the operator's ds-industry.css, font metrics READ FROM THE FONT rather than guessed, a deliberate '@internal shared sheet primitives for sibling assemblers' export block (render.ts:2802-2807), and eleven regression tests including a PDF-text decoder harness. TWO sibling documents already consume it without restyling. The operator's constraint is not at risk from adding a report - it is at risk only from someone adding a token or hard-coding a hex.

FLOOD 'PER-PARCEL COMPUTATION' IS REAL AND STRONGER THAN CLAIMED. It is a genuine D8 flow-accumulation hydrology run over a padded 3DEP catchment with live NOAA Atlas 14 rainfall (documented fallback to 9.5in when unavailable), producing catchment, drainage zones, ponding, flow paths, flow exits, a gradient raster and a prose briefing - and it persists BOTH a PDF and a machine-readable json-flood-drainage-study artifact. It requires NO warm/enriched parcel; it mints the parcel-terrain-model atom if absent. A feasibility study should read the persisted JSON artifact rather than re-run the DEM fetch.

COMPARE ALREADY EXISTS AS UI WITH NO EMITTER. CompareTool.tsx + compare-facts.ts ship a 2-slot, 7-row comparison with honest-absence cells and per-fact source captions - but zero export path (no pdf/export/download in the component). The later comparison report inherits a data model and a vocabulary, not a document. Do not let 'we already have compare' read as 'we already have a comparison report'.
